findings.why: TestApplyBatchFsync only asserts fsync_calls >= 1; does not verify the call happens before os.replace nor that the fd belongs to the temp file. A buggy implementation could fsync after replace (or on the wrong fd) and stay green, leaving FR-13/AD-8 unenforced.

TestApplyBatchInMemoryTailAfterBatch claims to verify apply_batch reloads tail_hash, but Ledger has no in-memory cache (append always reads from disk), so the test passes regardless of whether apply_batch reloads anything. The on-disk chain check is real; the 'reload' assertion is not.

_PROCESS_LOCK guards apply_batch only; Ledger.append does not acquire it. A concurrent append racing with apply_batch can have its bytes silently overwritten by apply_batch's os.replace. FR-8 says apply_batch MUST take the process-wide lock, but the module-scoped lock implies the intent was to cover all writes.
Uses tempfile.mkstemp + os.close + open(temp_path,'wb') rather than the AD-7 step 2 prescription of NamedTemporaryFile(mode='wb', delete=False, ...). Functionally equivalent but a spec deviation.

json.loads(raw) inside the existing-lines loop has no try/except; a single malformed byte in the existing JSONL causes the whole batch to raise JSONDecodeError rather than deferring to repair_tail (owned by STORY-03-02). Not exercised by ACs but unhandled.

For empty-ledger conflict (AC-3), pending_bytes is empty at the point of raise so no temp file is ever created; the tmp_files == [] assertion is structurally guaranteed, not behaviorally validated. A test case where validation succeeds for op 0 but fails for op 1 would catch a missing-cleanup regression.
No test exercises a delete op inside apply_batch, even though the implementation supports it (line 128-129). The delete conflict/replay semantics inside a batch are unverified.
